findings.falsification_reproduction: From repo root with Python 3.12: `python scripts/architecture_compliance_engine.py --json` (emits stdout only; no file writes). Observe score < 90 and L1-L5 FAIL. Then read `.github/workflows/foundation-gate.yml:3-6` to confirm no integration-branch trigger. Claim is falsified only if score >= 90 with zero FAILs AND the workflow triggers on this branch.
findings.root_cause: The compliance engine's rule allow-lists and layer model were not reconciled with the ~67-domain monorepo layout; the gate was wired only to `main`, so the integration branch accumulated 112 forbidden imports and 376 cross-domain violations without CI feedback.
findings.impact: Architecture governance is non-enforcing on the exact branch under audit. Any claim of 'architecture gate PASS' for this integration tree is unsupported by the engine's own output. Clean Architecture dependency direction is violated at scale (L1); domain boundaries are porous (L4). These are maintainability/regression risks, not evidence of a production defect by themselves.
findings.severity_rationale: HIGH: a hard gate that is declared in CI yet fails and does not run on the branch defeats the deterministic regression control; 376 cross-domain violations materially undermine the 11-domain isolation claim's enforceability.
findings.recommended_remediation: 1) Add the integration branch to foundation-gate.yml triggers (or create a branch-scoped gate) so the engine runs on every change. 2) Triage L3/L4 findings into a signed, committed baseline of acknowledged findings with a 'no new findings' diff-mode gate (as the sibling platform repo does). 3) Fix core->services inversion via ports/interfaces. 4) Record the resulting verdict as a new traceable record; do not self-award INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED.
alternatives: Lower the engine's FAIL threshold to WARNING and track as debt (weakens the gate; not recommended)
Adopt the sibling platform repo's baseline-gated architecture engine via a documented, owner-approved port instead of repairing L1-L7 allow-lists in place
findings.owner_gated_note: Engineering remediation; however ADR-A is BLOCKED and any architecture baseline policy change requires the named architecture/QA owner.

findings.title: Two mutually exclusive 'only authority' permission engines coexist (health_core vs NIAM/shared RBAC)
evidence: backend/app/health_core/authorization/engine.py:3 — docstring: 'The engine is the only authority for permissions.'
backend/app/health_core/authorization/guard.py:869 — engine=AuthorizationEngine(); :17 import from app.health_core.authorization.engine (only in-package instantiation)
grep 'health_core' in backend/app excluding health_core itself -> only 5 files, all under backend/app/interoperability/fhir_http/ (router.py, errors.py, security.py, repository.py, __init__.py)

backend/app/routes/authorization.py and backend/app/identity/services/authorization_service.py implement the main app authorization path (grep 'authorization_service|AuthorizationService' in backend/app, excluding health_core)

backend/app/domain_platform/shared_core.py:33-35 — catalog 'authorization' maps to backend/app/identity/services/authorization_service.py with description 'RBAC + ABAC + workspace-scoped permission checks.'
shared/rbac/permissions.py is imported by 4 backend/app files; backend/app/security/abac.py is cataloged as the ABAC provider
shared_core.py:17-19 — 'A service may appear here only if exactly ONE authoritative provider exists'
findings.falsification_reproduction: Compare the two docstrings/claims and their wiring: `grep -rn 'only authority' backend/app --include='*.py'`; `grep -rn 'AuthorizationEngine' backend/app --include='*.py'`; `grep -rn 'authorization_service' backend/app --include='*.py'`. If the health_core engine delegated to the NIAM service (or vice versa) through a single interface, the conflict would be falsified; it does not — the two are independent code paths with independent role/permission maps.
findings.root_cause: WS-A synthetic Health Core authorization slice was developed in parallel with the pre-existing NIAM identity/RBAC-ABAC authorization stack and never consolidated or explicitly scoped as synthetic-only.
findings.impact: Two independent permission maps can render divergent ALLOW/DENY decisions for the same principal; authorization drift and audit divergence are possible. Both claim exclusivity, so any reader must guess which is authoritative. Because health_core is only used by the non-activated FHIR HTTP test router, current production exposure is limited — but the architecture is ambiguous and unsafe to extend.
findings.severity_rationale: HIGH: authorization single-source-of-truth failure in a national health platform; likelihood MEDIUM because the second engine is currently confined to synthetic/non-activated surfaces.
findings.recommended_remediation: Designate one canonical authorization authority (recommended: cataloged backend/app/identity/services/authorization_service.py). Convert health_core AuthorizationEngine into a thin adapter that delegates to it, or explicitly rename/scope the docstring to 'synthetic Health Core only' and add a contract test proving decision equivalence. Update shared_core.py catalog to name the single authority and record an ADR.
alternatives: Keep both engines but add a differential test suite asserting identical decisions on a shared fixture corpus (does not eliminate drift risk)
Fully retire the health_core authorization engine and have fhir_http depend on the NIAM service (larger blast radius on synthetic evidence)
findings.owner_gated_note: true — identity/security owner; touches RBAC/ABAC and Shared Core canonical registry.

findings.root_cause: Domain packages grew by direct cross-imports rather than through interfaces/ports; startup/bootstrap code reaches into outer layers for worker and alert wiring; no enforced import-cycle gate on the integration branch (see AUD-ARCH-001).
findings.impact: Violates Clean Architecture dependency direction (innermost core importing outer services/lims); cycles prevent isolated domain testing and independent evolution, and weaken the claim that 11 canonical domains are independently certifiable. alternatives: Accept cycles as known debt in a signed baseline with a 'no new cycles' gate (lower cost, leaves coupling)
Reorganize into modules with literally independent package roots (high cost, high disruption)

findings.title: Constitution score baseline is stored in ephemeral /tmp, so regression protection is non-durable
evidence: scripts/constitution_enforcer.py:88 — SCORE_BASELINE_FILE = pathlib.Path('/tmp/constitution_baseline.json')
scripts/constitution_enforcer.py:675-697 — baseline read from /tmp, previous score compared, new score written back to /tmp
GOVERNANCE/NATIONAL_INTEGRATION/00_MASTER_EXECUTION_PLAN.md:76 — documents that prior /tmp/opencode artifacts were removed by an environment reset
git ls-files | grep -i baseline -> no committed constitution baseline JSON; only documentation baselines (EVIDENCE/BASELINE/BASELINE_REPORT.md, 01_PHASE_A_BASELINE.md)
findings.falsification_reproduction: Read scripts/constitution_enforcer.py:88 and check `git ls-files` for a tracked baseline JSON. If a durable, committed baseline existed and CI used it, the finding would be falsified. It does not.
findings.root_cause: Baseline persistence was implemented as a scratch file rather than a versioned repository artifact, so any environment reset silently resets the regression reference.
findings.impact: Score regressions cannot be reliably detected across environments/resets; a fresh CI runner has no baseline, weakening the constitution gate. Governance evidence is not reproducible.
findings.severity_rationale: MEDIUM: governance durability gap; no direct production runtime impact.
findings.recommended_remediation: Move the baseline to a tracked path (e.g. EVIDENCE/BASELINE/constitution_baseline.json) with deterministic content, read-only in CI diff mode; fail closed when the baseline is missing; document the update procedure.
alternatives: Inject the baseline as a CI secret/artifact (avoid: opaque and hard to review)
Recompute the baseline on every run and treat it as informational only (removes regression protection)
findings.owner_gated_note: false — engineering/CI fix, no owner-gated decision changed.
